sources.citation: Garellek, Marc & Patricia Keating. 2010. The acoustic consequences of phonation and tone interactions in Jalapa Mazatec. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 108: 143-163 [= Journal of the IPA 41(2): 185-205, 2011, doi:10.1017/S0025100311000193]
sources.note: Nothing on stress; background section covers the 3-way phonation x 3-way level tone system only. Sec. 2.2 notes that most target vowels were 'syllable-final' and that two breathy high-tone words were found only on 'non-word-final syllables' (methodology, not a stress rule).

sources.citation: Golston, Chris & Wolfgang Kehrein. 1998. Mazatec onsets and nuclei. International Journal of American Linguistics 64(4): 311-337
sources.note: Nothing; the paper treats Huautla and Jalapa syllable structure and phonation (citing Kirk, Ladefoged & Ladefoged 1993 for Jalapa); 'stress' occurs only in a reference title (Stark & Machin 1977 on Popoloca).

sources.citation: Silverman, Daniel, Barbara Blankenship, Paul Kirk & Peter Ladefoged. 1994. Phonetic structures in Jalapa Mazatec. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 87 (Fieldwork Studies of Targeted Languages II): 113-130 [= Anthropological Linguistics 37(1): 70-88, 1995]
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1 'Brief overview of phonology and morphology' (p. 113-114) gives syllable shape (maximally CCGV), three obligatory level tones, phonation contrasts, and 'Jalapa Mazatec roots are predominantly monosyllabic, while the rich inflectional system is by and large subsyllabic'; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the article (scanned of whole article checked, incl. loose spellings).
